 Blackcaps vs India: Four NZ wickets fall in opening session of first Test
 Sport Nation   •   November 19th, 2026 1:00 pm Henry Nicholls | Photo: Chris Symes/Photosport
 It was a horrific start to the first Test at the Basin Reserve for the Blackcaps - but a dream start for India. Tom Latham dismissed on just the third ball of play, leaving a delivery from Jasprit Bumrah that came back in to hit the New Zealand skipper's off stump and send him back to the pavilion without a run to his name. It didn't get much better for Latham's fellow opener Devon Conway. After a close call in the third over of the day where a caught behind call was wiped after video review, the next over, Anshul Kamboj made the second breakthrough of the opening session with Conway (4) caught behind by wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant to have NZ 12-2. With Rachin Ravindra's return from injury, in partnership for the third wicket with Henry Nicholls, the session calmed for the Blackcaps as they reached 50-2 by the 18th over with half an hour to play before the lunch break. But moments later, an edge off Ravindra's bat found the gloves of Pant on 15 runs with NZ now 51-3. The hurt didn't stop there however, with Daryl Mitchell (1) advancing down the pitch, but Bumrah's deliver found a thick inside edge to be caught brilliantly at short leg by Yashasvi Jaiswal. NZ struggling at 52-4 before reaching 60-4 as lunch is called. India dismiss the openers early in the first Test against NZ | Cricket Nation Gill wins toss to bowl first India captain Shubman Gill continues the trend of winning the toss during their tour of New Zealand. With Wellington's Basin Reserve ready to host the first Test, the visitors have elected to bowl first, sending in Blackcaps skipper Tom Latham and his opening partner Devon Conway. Blackcaps: Tom Latham (C), Devon Conway, Henry Nicholls, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Glenn Phillips, Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy India: KL Rahul, Yashavsi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Shubman Gill (C), Rishabh Pant (WK), Washington Sundar, Dhruv Jurel, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna Tune into Sport Nation for live and free ball-by-ball commentary throughout the first Test. Daniel McHardy leads the play-by-ball call, alongside Garth Gallaway. They're joined by experts Jeremy Coney, Grant Elliott, Kyle Mills for analysis, with Bharat Sundaresan set to join the team from Day 2 onwards. With Coney back, so is his ever-popular pitch report, thanks to PGG Wrightson Turf. How to sync live commentary on the Sport Nation app with your TV Head to sportnation.nz or open the Sport Nation app, select the match in the available streams and turn the volume up. Note: Most live sport will be on the main stream, but some events will be exclusively on Sport Nation Extra if there's a scheduling clash. 
 Tune into the same match on your TV (MySky) or video streaming app (SkyGo or Sky Sport Now) and turn up the volume. 
 For cricket, pause your TV or stream when you see/hear the bowler's front foot land during their delivery stride. For rugby league or football, pause your TV or stream when you hear the referee blow the whistle for the opening kick-off. 
 Listen to the Sport Nation stream, immediately unpause your TV or video stream when you hear the same sound (the scuff of the bowler's foot landing or referee's whistle) on the Sport Nation stream. Video and audio should now be in sync with each other, or at least very close to it. 
 If you're using a soundbar with your TV, the Sport Nation stream can be sent to it via Bluetooth.
